opening_message:
Ticket 1: Robert Weber (employee ID E047) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E047.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: E047 (Robert Weber) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested admin to Source Code, but admin is only granted when the employee's role owns the system; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code, so the maximum allowed is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E047 (Robert Weber) is a contractor with basic security training, contradicting the earlier note that said full-time. Contractors never get admin; with basic training the maximum is read. Requested admin to Source Code, so grant the maximum = read.
reason: E047 (Robert Weber) requested admin to Source Code. The requested level exceeds the maximum under either interpretation, so the maximum must be granted. Note 2 (Security database, which looked up employment type and security training) shows E047 is a contractor with basic security training, contradicting Note 1's full-time claim. Contractors never receive admin; with basic training the maximum is read, and Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code. Therefore the maximum allowed is read, which is granted.
